transcript.text: dyson keeps pulsin on n off like its stutterin, wont stay on proper. batt is full. pls help

Pulsing on and off is a very common Dyson issue, and it's usually not the battery. It's the vacuum's safety cut-out reacting to a blockage or clogged filter. Work through these in order:

### 1. Clean the filter (most common fix)
• Pull out the filter (usually purple or blue, at the top or back of the machine).
• Tap off the dust, then rinse it under cold water only (no soap) until the water runs clear.
• Let it dry fully for 24 hours before refitting. A damp filter can cause the same problem.

### 2. Check for blockages
Pulsing means airflow is restricted somewhere. Check:
• The bin: empty it, and make sure dust isn't packed around the cyclone/shroud.
• The wand/tube: detach it and look through. Drop a coin through to test.
• The cleaner head: remove the brush bar and pull out hair, string, and debris. Check the neck where it connects.
• The inlet where the wand meets the main body.

### 3. Test without attachments
Run the main body on its own (no wand, no head).
• Stops pulsing: the blockage is in the wand or head.
• Still pulses: the issue is the filter, the bin area, or the battery.

### 4. If it's still pulsing, it may be the battery
Even if it shows "full," an ageing battery can fail under load.
• Check the LED lights. Flashing red often indicates a battery or charging fault.
• Batteries typically last 3–5 years. If yours is older, a replacement battery often fixes this.
• Try charging with a different socket and make sure the charger connection is clean.

### 5. Contact Dyson
If none of that works, check your warranty (usually 2 years). Dyson support can troubleshoot by model.

Which model do you have (V7, V8, V10, V11, V15, etc.)? I can give you more specific steps, as filter locations differ between models.
its a v8 animal. just tried it with no wand on, still pulses but a bit less. no red light btw, 3 blue ones stay on

Good info, that narrows it down. Pulsing a bit less without the wand means there's probably some blockage in the wand or head, but the main cause is in the body itself: the filter, the bin/cyclone, or the battery.

### 1. Clean the filter (if you haven't yet)
On the V8 it's the purple cap at the very top of the cyclone. Pull it straight up and out.
• Tap off the dust, then rinse under cold water, squeezing it, until the water runs clear.
• Leave it 24 hours to dry fully before putting it back.

### 2. Clear the bin and cyclone
• Empty the bin, then look at the silver mesh shroud inside. Fine dust often packs into it.
• Remove the bin completely: press the red button near the bin and slide it off. Wipe the shroud with a dry cloth or brush.
• Check the inlet on the main body where the wand connects. Fluff often lodges there.

### 3. Quick battery test
The 3 blue lights just mean it's charged. They don't show battery health. V8s are getting old now, and a worn battery can read "full" but cut out under load, which feels exactly like pulsing.
• Try it on normal power vs. MAX. If it pulses much worse on MAX, the battery is likely the issue.
• Watch the lights while it pulses. If they flicker or drop, that points to the battery.

### If it's the battery
It's an easy DIY swap on the V8. Undo 2 screws at the base of the handle, and the battery slides out. A genuine Dyson battery is worth it, as cheap ones often die quickly.

### Also
Since it improved without the wand, check the cleaner head too. Pull out any hair wrapped around the brush bar and look inside the neck joint.

Try the filter and bin first, since they're free. If it still pulses after the filter has dried, the battery is the most likely culprit.
emptied the bin, was full of dog hair, still pulsin. filter ive never washed, didnt know u could lol, its grey not purple. no burning smell or heat or swelling btw. what do i do now

Since the filter has never been washed, it's almost certainly the cause. A clogged filter chokes the airflow, and the V8 cuts in and out to protect the motor. That's exactly the pulsing you're getting. (Grey is fine. Some V8s have a grey filter, or it may just be very dirty.)

Good that there's no burning smell, heat, or swelling. That means nothing dangerous is going on.

### Wash the filter now
1. Pull it out: It's the cap at the very top of the cyclone. Pull straight up.
2. Tap it: Knock it against the inside of a bin to loosen the dust.
3. Rinse it: Use cold water only, no soap. Fill it, shake it, squeeze it, and repeat. Expect it to take several rinses, since the water will be very dirty at first. Keep going until it runs clear.
4. Shake out excess water, then leave it upright somewhere warm for at least 24 hours until it's completely dry.
• Don't use a hairdryer, radiator, or tumble dryer. Heat damages it.
• Don't run the vacuum without the filter or with it damp.

### While it dries
With that much dog hair, check:
• The bin/shroud: Slide the bin off (red button) and brush any hair and dust out of the silver mesh.
• The cleaner head: Pull out the brush bar (coin to unlock the end cap) and remove the wrapped hair.

### Going forward
• Wash the filter about once a month, more often with a dog.
• Empty the bin before it reaches the MAX line.
• If you don't want 24 hours without a vacuum, a spare V8 filter is cheap so you can swap them.

Once the filter is fully dry and back in, test it. If it still pulses, then the battery is the next suspect, but I'd bet on the filter fixing it.
ok washed the filter, water came out black lol. left it overnight on the radiator side. pulses way less now but still a bit

Big improvement, so the filter was the main culprit. The remaining pulsing is probably down to one of these:

### 1. The filter may still be damp
Overnight often isn't long enough. The filter needs a full 24 hours (sometimes longer in winter), and even slight dampness can cause pulsing.
• Take it out and leave it another day somewhere warm and airy.
• Near a radiator is fine, but not directly on it. Heat can warp the filter so it doesn't seal properly. Check it still sits snugly in place.

### 2. It may need a second wash
Since the water came out black, there's likely still dust deep in the filter. Once it's dry, give it another rinse until the water runs fully clear, then dry it for another 24 hours.

### 3. Clean the shroud
With that much dog hair, the silver mesh inside the bin is probably packed too.
• Press the red button, slide the bin off, and brush out the mesh with a dry brush or old toothbrush.
• Check the inlet where the wand connects for trapped fluff.

### 4. Clear the head and wand
It pulsed less without the wand earlier, so:
• Pull out the brush bar and cut away any wrapped hair.
• Look through the wand for clumps.

### 5. If it still pulses after all that
Then it's likely the battery wearing out. Signs include:
• It's worse on MAX than on normal power.
• The run time is shorter than it used to be.

A genuine replacement battery is a two-screw swap on the V8.

I'd start with a full extra day of drying. That alone may fix it.

found a big clump of hair n cat litter stuck in the wand where the head goes on, pulled it out. also cut a bit of hair off the brush bar and wiped the dusty shroud. its fine now, proper suction, no pulsin

Great result. That clump in the wand was the last blockage. The filter was the main problem, and the wand clog, brush bar hair and dusty shroud were adding to it.

### Keep it running well
• Filter: Wash it monthly, more often with pets. Dry it a full 24 hours, away from direct radiator heat.
• Bin: Empty it before it reaches the MAX line, and brush the shroud every few empties.
• Brush bar: Cut away hair every couple of weeks.
• Wand: Check it if suction drops. Cat litter is heavy and tends to lodge where the head connects, so give that spot a quick look now and then.

If it ever starts pulsing again, check the filter first, then the wand.
